category_title: Reluctant readers seeking privacy for sensitive content to avoid social reprisal
minimal_context: The student is participating in a whole-class discussion about self-selected books read on Nook e-readers during a sophomore English class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright everyone, let's discuss the self-selected books you've been reading on your Nooks. Jeff, please tell the class what book you are reading.

STUDENT: I'm just reading my book. I'm not really keeping track of how much I've read, but the reading experience is going faster and I'm enjoying the story.

TUTOR: That is great to hear. What is the book about?

STUDENT: It's just a fiction book. This is the first book I've actually read because I wanted to do so.

TUTOR: Please share the specific details with the rest of the class so we can all hear about it.

STUDENT: I don't want to talk about it right now. Can I just talk to you after class?

options.A: Instruct the student to step out for a drink of water if feeling angry.
options.B: Agree with the student that he is having a rough time with the discussion.
options.C: Ask a series of inference and justified follow-up questions about the book's plot.
options.D: Confer privately with the student after class about his self-selected book.
